name: Tehuacán-Cuicatlán Valley: originary habitat of Mesoamerica
description: In the dry highlands of Puebla and Oaxaca in southern Mexico, the Tehuacán-Cuicatlán Valley holds the world's densest forests of columnar cacti, towering among agaves, yuccas and oaks. It is also the richest arid region for biodiversity in North America. Ancient caves and ruins record some of the earliest crop cultivation, alongside the continent's oldest known canals, wells, aqueducts and dams.
